subject: Recap: multi-tenant rate model & quota needs — CloudNova discovery
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Chen <sofia.chen@cloudnova.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Recap: multi-tenant rate model & quota needs — CloudNova discovery

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and the proposed immediate next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain points you mentioned:
- High variance in per-customer traffic: a small number of tenants are generating most of the token spend and causing tail latency spikes.
- Need for per-customer routing policy (tiered capacity) so premium customers get lower-latency paths.
- Enforceable rate limits and quotas at tenant level (minute/hour/day) for billing predictability and abuse control.
- Want safeguards for cost (token caps / alerts) and a way to throttle without dropping requests entirely.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Serving on EKS with a mix of in-house microservices and third-party LLM APIs for prototyping.
- Auth & tenant mapping in a central gateway; usage events flow to your billing pipeline (Kafka -> Redshift).

Success criteria you called out:
1) Per-tenant rate limiting and tiering implemented for top 3 customer tiers.
2) <200ms P95 latency for premium route under typical load.
3) Ability to set per-tenant token/day budget and automated throttling/notifications.
4) Pilot with 5 tenants for 6 weeks, measurable cost delta and latency improvement.

Suggested next steps (short timeline):
- Technical deep dive (45m) next week with your infra and security folks to validate integration points (pref: Dec 9–10).
- Share a short one-pager on Redwood multi-tenant controls (attached).
- I will send two rate-model options (conservative / aggressive) for your review before the deep dive.

Attachments: redwood-tenant-controls-onepager.pdf (one-pager summary of per-tenant controls and common deployment patterns)

If that matches your understanding, I’ll lock in a time and loop in Vanessa (SE) for the deep dive.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Recap: multi-tenant rate model & quota needs — CloudNova discovery

Alex — thanks, that lines up well with our notes. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Premium customers are ~5% of tenants but ~65% of spend — so routing/tiering is priority #1.
- For quotas, we need both soft throttles (queue/slowdown) and hard caps (reject) depending on tenant tier.
- Security team wants to be part of the deep dive to validate data residency and audit log needs. I copied them here.

Can you include a sample rate table (tokens/min per tier) in the model options? Also include expected cost delta if we route lower-tier tenants to quantized models.

— Sofia
Sofia Chen

sofia.chen@cloudnova.com

Subject: Re: Recap: multi-tenant rate model & quota needs — CloudNova discovery

Sofia — attached is a short spreadsheet (cloudnova-rate-model-options.xlsx) with two starter rate models plus an ROI sketch. Highlights: 

Option A (conservative):
- Tier 1 (premium): 6,000 tokens/minute, guaranteed route to low-latency pool.
- Tier 2 (standard): 1,500 tokens/minute, dynamic batching enabled.
- Tier 3 (developer): 500 tokens/minute, default to quantized model by policy.
- Soft throttle window: gradual request slowdown over 30s before hard reject.

Option B (aggressive cost-savings):
- Smaller guaranteed capacity for lower tiers; aggressive routing of non-interactive workloads to quantized variants.
- Day-level token caps with automated notifications + temporary hold.

Estimated outcomes: reduced peak cost by 18–32% depending on traffic mix; expected improvement in P95 latency for Tier 1 under 20%–40% depending on autoscaling headroom.

Next actions I propose:
1) Technical deep dive with your infra + security (45m) — propose Wed Dec 9 10:00–10:45 PT or Thu Dec 10 11:00–11:45 PT. Which works?
2) If deep dive looks good, we’ll scope a 6-week pilot and lock a pilot SLO (latency & cost targets).

Deal reference: DN-43821 — I’ll update HubSpot after we confirm the deep dive.

Attachment: cloudnova-rate-model-options.xlsx

Best,
Alex

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Michael Lee <michael.lee@cloudnova.com>, sec-team@cloudnova.com
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Recap: multi-tenant rate model & quota needs — CloudNova discovery

Hi Sofia / team — Vanessa here (sales engineer). A couple quick technical notes ahead of the deep dive so the conversation can be focused: 

- Routing: we can implement policy-based routing (tier => pool) at the request gateway with fallback rules. We recommend a small low-latency pool pinned to premium tenants and a shared pool for standard tenants.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts will reduce tokens and latency for high-volume tenants; easy to enable per-tenant.
- Quotas: Redwood supports hard quotas + soft throttles with customizable grace windows and webhook notifications for billing.
- Security/audit: we produce per-request audit logs + KMS integrations; we’ll bring our compliance lead if you want SOC2 artifact mapping.

Proposed deep dive slots (Vanessa / Alex / infra + security):
- Wed Dec 9 — 10:00–10:45 PT
- Thu Dec 10 — 11:00–11:45 PT

I’ve added a short internal playbook link here that outlines implementation patterns: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/tenant-controls-playbook

Please confirm which slot works and if you want us to invite our compliance lead. Looking forward to the next step.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
